owns: External content synchronization (Google Drive, OneDrive, cloud content)
dependsOn: Search / AIML service — generic search, content ingestion
Rendition service — PDF/image rendition HTTP client
Page Storage service — HTML page blob storage
User Management Service (UMS) — user lookup, permission
Google Drive API — OAuth2 + Drive sync

gapAnalysis.title: Anemic domain model — FileEntity/ItemModel has zero behavior
gapAnalysis.detail: ItemModel is a 90+ property data bag with public setters and no methods. All business rules that should live on the aggregate (checkout guard, delete guard, rename uniqueness, folder-type guard) are implemented as static methods in FileWriter.cs and FileCheckpoint.cs. State mutations such as setting checkout status or soft-deleting are performed directly on the DTO by the writer layer with no invariant protection.

gapAnalysis.title: Business logic in application layer — ActivationWriter enforces domain invariants
gapAnalysis.detail: ActivationWriter.ActivateContents contains multi-line domain rules: it checks item.VersionActivationStage == ContentVersionStatus.Published to throw ActivateActivatedVersionException, verifies variant uniqueness via LINQ GroupBy, and enforces the primary-version-must-exist rule. These are domain invariants that must be enforced inside ContentVersionEntity aggregate methods.

gapAnalysis.title: Static writer/reader classes bypass DI — untestable and uninjectable
gapAnalysis.detail: FileWriter, ActivationWriter, RenameItemCommon, FolderWriter and 15+ other writer classes are static. Controllers call them directly (FileWriter.AddFile(), FileWriter.DeleteFile()). Context and orchestrators are created via OrchestratorFactory and new ScopedExpressContext() inside the static methods. This makes business logic untestable in isolation and impossible to mock, and means DI-registered services cannot be substituted.

gapAnalysis.title: Domain repositories contain raw SQL — infrastructure leaks into domain layer
gapAnalysis.detail: FileRepository, ItemRepository, FolderRepository, and 27 other repositories extend SQLDataRepository and embed raw T-SQL strings with SqlParameter arrays. The repositories are located in the domain project (LibraryService.Domain) but are tightly coupled to SQL Server. There is no query abstraction; changing persistence requires touching domain-layer files.

gapAnalysis.title: Checkpoint classes externally enforce invariants that belong on aggregates
gapAnalysis.detail: 30+ *Checkpoint.cs classes in Express.Orchestrator/Checkpoint/ validate preconditions and throw exceptions before reaching any domain object. E.g. FileCheckpoint throws FileNotFoundException, FolderCheckpoint throws NoPermissionException. These are domain invariants; they should be enforced by aggregate methods, not by separate static validation classes upstream.

gapAnalysis.title: ContentEventConsumer uses fire-and-forget Task.Factory.StartNew with no await
gapAnalysis.detail: ContentEventConsumer.ConsumeEvent spawns a LongRunning Task via Task.Factory.StartNew with _ = discarding the task handle. Exceptions inside RunConsumeAsync are caught only at the inner retry loop; an uncaught exception silently kills the consumer. Additionally Kafka offset is committed unconditionally (subscriber.Value.Commit called outside the tenant-match branch), meaning events for other tenants are silently dropped but their offsets advance.

gapAnalysis.title: Invariants enforced outside aggregates
gapAnalysis.detail: All domain invariant checks (file writable, file locked, file belongs to team site, version expirable) live in SystemStateExecutor and FileWriter rather than inside aggregate methods on FileEntity or FileVersionEntity. This means the rules can be bypassed by calling the repository directly.

gapAnalysis.title: Business logic in Express Writer layer
gapAnalysis.detail: FileWriter, PublishWriter, and ActivationWriter contain branching business logic (publishability checks, checkout ownership, custom property validation) that belongs in domain aggregate methods. These classes act as a de-facto domain layer without the encapsulation guarantees.

gapAnalysis.title: State transitions set externally on entities
gapAnalysis.detail: Workflow status (SUBMITTED, REJECTED, PROMOTED) and system state flags are set directly on model properties from application-layer code (e.g. item.WorkflowStatus = STATUS_SUBMITTED) rather than through protected aggregate command methods that enforce valid transitions.

gapAnalysis.title: Service Locator anti-pattern
gapAnalysis.detail: ServiceCollectionHelper.GetSingletonService<T> and GetScopedService<T> are used throughout FileWriter and OrchestratorFactory to resolve dependencies at runtime, creating hidden coupling and making unit testing impossible without the full DI container.

gapAnalysis.title: OrchestratorFactory hides 30+ implementations
gapAnalysis.detail: OrchestratorFactory creates orchestrators for 30+ operation types behind a single factory method. Actual dependencies (repositories, providers, Kafka clients) are invisible at the composition root, making static analysis and testing extremely difficult.

gapAnalysis.title: Service locator used throughout instead of constructor injection
gapAnalysis.detail: ServiceCollectionHelper.GetSingletonService<T>() is called 1,482 times across the codebase (SearchProducer.cs, ContentEventConsumer.cs, and hundreds of Reader/Writer classes). This is a well-known anti-pattern that defeats IoC, makes unit testing impossible, and hides dependencies. Every class resolves its own dependencies at runtime rather than declaring them via constructor parameters.

gapAnalysis.title: Static Reader/Writer classes replace application services and domain objects
gapAnalysis.detail: 70+ Reader and Writer classes (FileWriter, FolderWriter, PublishWriter, ActivationWriter, PermissionWriter, ExtensiveFileWriter, SBPProfileWriter, etc.) are used as static-style facades called directly from controllers (e.g. FileController.cs calls FileWriter.AddFile(), FileReader.ReadUnifiedContents()). These classes contain thousands of lines of mixed business logic, validation, persistence calls, and Kafka publishing. There is no application service layer or domain model layer — all behavior lives in these Reader/Writer monoliths.

gapAnalysis.title: Domain entity status mutated directly outside aggregate
gapAnalysis.detail: Content item status is mutated directly on model objects in Writer classes rather than through aggregate command methods. Examples: ExternalSyncWriter.cs line 204 (itemVersion.Status = STATUS_UPLOAD_VIDEO_FOUNDATION_PROCESS_STREAM), line 211 (itemVersion.Status = isOfficeDocOrMedia ? ... : STATUS_READY), FileVersionWriter.cs line 1570 (newArticleVersion.Status = ItemStatus.STATUS_READY), SBPProfileWriter.cs lines 1423-1537 (repeated status checks and mutations). No invariant protection around state transitions.

gapAnalysis.title: Validation scattered across 40+ Checkpoint classes instead of aggregate invariants
gapAnalysis.detail: Business validation rules are encoded in 40+ procedural Checkpoint classes in the Orchestrator project (FileCheckpoint, FilePublishableCheckpoint, FileDeletableCheckpoint, ActivateCheckpoint, PromoteCheckpoint, FolderDeletableCheckpoint, ItemNameTooLongCheckpoint, etc.). These checkpoints execute guard logic that belongs inside aggregate command methods. The result is that business rules can be bypassed by calling Writer methods without running the associated checkpoints.

gapAnalysis.title: Two incompatible exception hierarchies with no typed DomainExceptionType
gapAnalysis.detail: The codebase has two distinct exception bases: ContentManagerException in ControlCenter.Core.Exceptions.Common (with ContentManagerExceptionCategory enum: Unknown/NotFound/InvalidParamter/NoPermission/ServiceUnavaliable/WorkflowDisabled) and ContentManagerException in LibraryService.Abstractions.Exceptions. Neither maps cleanly to HTTP status codes through a single DomainExceptionType enum. 150+ specific exception classes exist but are thrown from all layers including domain, infrastructure, and even controllers.

gapAnalysis.title: Controllers bypass application service layer and call Reader/Writer directly
gapAnalysis.detail: Controllers across all API versions (V1.0, V1.1, V2.0, Unified, Orbit, APIM, Dark) resolve business operations by directly instantiating or calling static-style Reader/Writer classes. Example: FileController (V1.0) calls FileVersionReader.ReadLatestVersion() and FileWriter.AddFile() with no intervening application service. FileController (Unified) calls FileReader.ReadUnifiedContents() and ExtensiveFileWriter.AddContent(). This means controllers contain implicit orchestration logic.

gapAnalysis.title: Domain project contains infrastructure concerns
gapAnalysis.detail: The Domain project houses infrastructure classes: NodeRepository (SQL queries), GoogleDriveRepository, ExternalSyncRepository, UserSettingRepository, SearchProducer (Kafka publisher), CacheRemoverClient (HTTP calls), ExternalSyncService (orchestration), MicroAppRepository. None of these belong in a domain project — they are infrastructure adapters. The real domain has no home.

gapAnalysis.title: Static Writer/Reader classes replace injectable Application Services
gapAnalysis.detail: Business logic lives in ~45 static classes (FileWriter, PublishWriter, FolderWriter, ContentViewReader, etc.) inside Seismic.ContentManager.Express. These classes create their own context via `new ScopedExpressContext()` inline and resolve dependencies via ServiceCollectionHelper service locator. They cannot be unit tested, mocked, or decorated. Every 'application service' method is a static entry point rather than a proper injectable IFileAppService/IPublishAppService.

gapAnalysis.title: Service Locator anti-pattern via ServiceCollectionHelper
gapAnalysis.detail: ServiceCollectionHelper.GetSingletonService<T>() and GetScopedService<T>() are called in ContentViewReader (~15 calls), ContentEventConsumer, FileWriter, and other static Express classes. This hides dependencies, makes constructor injection impossible, and breaks testability. The ILogger, ISeismicCacheProvider, IToggle, IFMSClientManager, and IMapperService are all resolved at call time rather than at construction time.

gapAnalysis.title: Anemic domain model — no aggregate roots with invariant methods
gapAnalysis.detail: FileManager, ItemManager are single-method thin delegators to repositories. FileVersionManager has no version state-transition methods. No entity class enforces business rules. All invariants (file cannot be published if checked out, version minorVersion != 0 blocks publish, name uniqueness) live in Checkpoint classes or Writer static methods rather than on aggregate root methods. ContentObjectStatus is a string-constants class rather than a typed enum or value object with valid-transition enforcement.

gapAnalysis.title: Business invariants enforced in Orchestrator Checkpoint layer instead of domain
gapAnalysis.detail: Seismic.ContentManager.Express.Orchestrator contains 40+ Checkpoint classes (FilePublishableCheckpoint, FolderOperableCheckpoint, PromoteCheckpoint, RenameCheckpoint, etc.) that enforce domain invariants — existence checks, permission gates, state pre-conditions — by throwing typed exceptions. These rules belong as guard methods on aggregate roots (e.g. FileEntity.Publish(), FolderEntity.Rename()). Moving them into the domain makes invariants co-located with state and testable without the full orchestrator stack.

gapAnalysis.title: No DomainException base class — 280+ raw exception types with no unified HTTP mapping
gapAnalysis.detail: All domain exceptions (FileNotFoundException, NoPermissionException, ActivateActivatedVersionException, etc.) extend System.Exception or application-specific bases with no shared DomainException<DomainExceptionType> contract. HTTP status code mapping is scattered across exception handlers. Adding a new exception requires updating multiple middleware layers. There is no DomainExceptionType enum to centralise code-to-HTTP mapping.

gapAnalysis.title: OrchestratorFactory static factory bypasses DI — 40+ orchestrators uninjectable
gapAnalysis.detail: OrchestratorFactory.Create*Orchestrator() methods construct orchestrators by resolving services via ServiceCollectionHelper.GetSingletonService() (a service locator). This means orchestrators depend on ambient static state, cannot be substituted in tests, and their dependency graph is invisible to the DI container. 40+ orchestrator interfaces are registered in DI but never actually injected — they are retrieved via the factory.

gapAnalysis.title: No value objects — status, tenant identity, and compound keys represented as raw primitives
gapAnalysis.detail: Content status is a raw string (item.Status = "published"), tenant identity is a raw string (teamSiteId), and compound version identity (contentId + versionId + variantId) is passed as separate string parameters everywhere. There are no immutable value objects with validation rules or equality semantics. This allows invalid states (e.g. empty status string, mismatched tenant) to propagate silently through the domain.

gapAnalysis.title: ScopedExpressContext created with 'new' inside writers — ambient tenant context not injected
gapAnalysis.detail: Every static writer method creates context via new ScopedExpressContext() or new WorkerExpressContext(tenantInfo, userId). This pulls current tenant/user from ambient thread state rather than from a well-defined IExpressContext injected through the request pipeline. Multi-tenancy correctness depends on thread-local state being set correctly upstream, which is fragile and invisible in tests.

gapAnalysis.title: Domain events not raised by aggregates — side effects triggered imperatively in writers
gapAnalysis.detail: After state changes (file deleted, content activated, content expired) the writers imperatively call observer/producer classes (LibraryContentReferencesObserver.Notify(), SearchProducer.Publish(), DataCollectionObserver.Notify()). There is no domain event raised from an aggregate method that the application service then dispatches. Side effect ordering and completeness depend on each writer remembering to call the right observers.

gapAnalysis.title: ExpirationJobExecutor and processor classes contain domain expiry rules
gapAnalysis.detail: ContentExpireProcessor and ContentExpireNotifyProcessor determine expiry thresholds and notification timing using SQL queries and inline logic rather than through a domain object method. The rule 'notify N days before expiration' is a domain invariant that should live on ContentExpirationEntity, not in a background job executor.

gapAnalysis.title: ScopedExpressContext couples domain to HTTP
gapAnalysis.detail: ScopedExpressContext holds a reference to the HTTP HttpContext as well as user identity, tenant info, permissions, and feature toggle state. Domain operations that accept this context are tightly coupled to ASP.NET Core middleware, preventing reuse in background services and tests.

gapAnalysis.title: ExpirationJobExecutor accesses warehouse SQL directly
gapAnalysis.detail: ExpirationJobExecutor calls into the Warehouse SQL layer directly with raw Dapper queries to find and expire versions, bypassing the domain aggregate and repository interfaces defined in the abstraction layer.

gapAnalysis.title: No aggregate root boundary on content graph
gapAnalysis.detail: File, FileVersion, FileVariant, FileAnnotation, and CustomPropertyValues are accessed independently through separate repositories. There is no aggregate root that controls the transactional boundary, allowing partial updates that can leave the content graph in inconsistent state.

gapAnalysis.title: Custom property validation in wrong layer
gapAnalysis.detail: CustomPropertyInvalidCheck and PropertyValueCalculatorUtils.BatchCalculatePropertyValues() are invoked from FileWriter (application layer) rather than from within the CustomPropertyEntity or a CustomPropertyDomainService, leaking domain validation into the orchestration layer.

gapAnalysis.title: Raw exceptions not mapped through DomainExceptionType
gapAnalysis.detail: Several classes throw raw framework exceptions (InvalidOperationException, ArgumentException, generic Exception) instead of typed ContentManagerException subclasses, causing HTTP status code decisions to be made inconsistently at the controller and middleware level.

gapAnalysis.title: Multiple API version controllers duplicating logic
gapAnalysis.detail: V1.0, V1.1, V2.0, V3.0 plus Dark/Orbit/APIM variants create 80+ controller classes with overlapping endpoint implementations. Cross-version logic differences are managed with if-branches and conditional DI rather than versioned application services.

gapAnalysis.title: Kafka event listeners contain domain logic instead of delegating to domain services
gapAnalysis.detail: ContentEventConsumer, CustomPropertyEventListener, VFSEventListener, CrackingPipelineMetaEventListener, and AugmentationEventListener handle Kafka events using ServiceCollectionHelper.GetSingletonService<T>() and contain inline domain logic. They do not delegate to domain services or command handlers. VFSEventListener directly transitions file version status on video-processed events.

gapAnalysis.title: Missing value objects — status, type, and identity fields are raw primitives
gapAnalysis.detail: Content status values are compared as raw string literals and integer constants (e.g. 'if (item.Status == ContentObjectStatus.STATUS_GOOGLEDRIVE_PLACE_HOLDER)' scattered across 10+ Writer files). ContentType, Language, TenantId, TeamSiteId, and ContentId are all raw strings or GUIDs with no encapsulating value object enforcing validity. ContentObjectStatus is used as an enum but its transitions are not protected by a state machine.

gapAnalysis.title: Common.Model project is a 500+ file shared DTO dumping ground
gapAnalysis.detail: Common.Model contains 523+ files with all DTOs, request/response models, and shared constants mixed together with no domain separation. This creates implicit coupling across all bounded contexts — any model change risks breaking unrelated domains. There is no separation between domain model objects and API view models.

gapAnalysis.title: PropertyMessageController is a 432-line orchestration class in the controller layer
gapAnalysis.detail: PropertyMessageController performs complex nested-loop orchestration, maintains intermediate state, and executes multi-step batch custom property processing directly in controller action methods. This is orchestration that belongs in an application service or domain service.

gapAnalysis.title: No domain events raised on state transitions — search indexing is a direct call
gapAnalysis.detail: SearchProducer.ProduceAsync() is called directly from Writer classes without a domain event intermediary. When a file is published or activated, the Writer directly calls SearchProducer rather than raising a domain event (ContentPublished, ContentActivated) that a handler forwards to search. This couples business operations to infrastructure concerns and makes it impossible to add additional side effects without modifying Writer classes.
gapAnalysis.file: SearchProducer.cs (called directly from multiple Writer classes)

gapAnalysis.title: Seismic.ContentManager.Express.Orchestrator is a mixed-layer project
gapAnalysis.detail: The Orchestrator project mixes: Checkpoint validation classes (domain invariant logic), Orchestrator interfaces for HTTP clients (infrastructure), Cart and context-passing classes (application layer), and SQL orchestrators (infrastructure queries). It is a catch-all that prevents proper layer separation.

gapAnalysis.title: ExternalSyncService and ContentSyncManager coordinate sync without a domain abstraction
gapAnalysis.detail: ExternalSyncService.cs and ContentSyncManager.cs (in the Domain project) orchestrate multi-step external sync workflows procedurally. ContentSyncManager.cs line 282 catches ContentManagerException inline and branches business flow on exception type rather than on explicit domain state. This is infrastructure logic disguised as domain logic.

gapAnalysis.title: Domain project (LibraryService.Domain) contains HTTP client implementations
gapAnalysis.detail: RenditionHttpClient, PageStorageClient, DiscEventV2Client, GoogleDriveManager+AuthClient all live inside Seismic.ContentManagerService.LibraryService.Domain. A domain project must not contain HTTP clients or external-system coupling. These should live in an Infrastructure project with interfaces defined in the domain contracts.

gapAnalysis.title: ContentEventConsumer uses static fields and service locator instead of BackgroundService DI
gapAnalysis.detail: ContentEventConsumer is a static class with static Lazy<> Kafka subscriber fields and static ILogger resolved via ServiceCollectionHelper. It lacks BackgroundService lifecycle management. Other listeners (CustomPropertyEventListener, VFSEventListener) follow a slightly better pattern but still use static subscriber dictionaries. All Kafka consumers should implement BackgroundService with constructor-injected IAvroClientFactory, IServiceScopeFactory, and ILogger.

gapAnalysis.title: Kafka publish embedded in Observer pattern inside Express — not domain events
gapAnalysis.detail: EventBusObserver, SearchMeshObserver, WebhookEventObserver, LibraryContentReferencesObserver, DataCollectionObserver all live in Seismic.ContentManager.Express/Notification. They are called from within Writers via a notification chain. The domain events they represent (ContentPublished, ContentDeleted, ContentUpdated) are not first-class domain event objects — they are constructed inline with raw data mapping inside the observer, making it impossible to test domain event semantics independently.

gapAnalysis.title: OrchestratorFactory uses static factory methods creating deep object graphs
gapAnalysis.detail: OrchestratorFactory.CreateTeamSiteOrchestrator(context), CreatePublishOrchestrator(context), etc. are static factory methods used inside every Writer. These factories create new orchestrator instances per call, bypassing DI lifetime management and making it impossible to swap implementations for testing without modifying static code.

gapAnalysis.title: Kafka consumer group ID uses non-production naming convention
gapAnalysis.detail: ContentEventConsumer creates a consumer group with GroupId = cms-test-consumer-{topic}. The 'test' infix in a production consumer group ID risks conflicting with actual test consumers and makes observability tooling harder to distinguish environments.

gapAnalysis.title: RLPolling background service uses Thread.Sleep instead of async delay
gapAnalysis.detail: ExpirationBackgroundService calls Thread.Sleep(sleepMillis) inside an async ExecuteAsync method, blocking the thread pool thread for the sleep duration. Should use await Task.Delay() to release the thread during idle periods.

gapAnalysis.title: Orchestrator layer duplicates permission checking already done in controllers
gapAnalysis.detail: Multiple orchestrators re-validate permissions (tenant access, user role) that are already enforced by the [Authorize] attribute and policy middleware on the controller. This creates divergence risk: a permission change must be applied in two places.

gapAnalysis.title: WorkflowRequestProxy is a pure HTTP passthrough
gapAnalysis.detail: WorkflowRequestProxy contains zero domain logic — it is a typed HTTP client masquerading as a domain service. Local workflow status is not enforced: the service cannot protect against invalid status transitions when the external workflow service is unavailable.

gapAnalysis.title: No domain events raised internally
gapAnalysis.detail: The service publishes Kafka events after persistence but raises no in-process domain events. This means cross-domain reactions (e.g. expiration triggers permission cleanup) must be handled by the application layer, creating temporal coupling and making side-effect chains hard to trace.

gapAnalysis.title: Batch operations allow partial failure silently
gapAnalysis.detail: BatchUpdateFileCustomProperties catches per-item exceptions and continues, returning a mixed success/failure result without any rollback of prior successful items. There is no compensating transaction or saga to restore consistency on partial failure.

gapAnalysis.title: Tenant context passed as parameter, not encapsulated
gapAnalysis.detail: tenantId and teamSiteId are passed as explicit parameters through every method call stack rather than being encapsulated in a TenantContext value object resolved once at the request boundary. This causes widespread coupling to multi-tenancy infrastructure in domain methods.

gapAnalysis.title: RenditionReader sets Rendition status directly on view model during read
gapAnalysis.detail: RenditionReader.cs lines 178, 204, 212, 216 set skimmer.Status = RENDITION_STATUS.READY/PROCESSING/NOTEXIST directly inside a read operation while mapping data. Status derivation logic for rendition availability belongs in a RenditionEntity or domain service, not in a reader/mapping class.

gapAnalysis.title: Tabeeb.Business.Domain and Tabeeb.Business.Common are orphaned external domain fragments
gapAnalysis.detail: Two projects (Tabeeb.Business.Domain, Tabeeb.Business.Common) exist as source code within the service repo but represent a different product domain (Tabeeb). These should either be extracted to their own service or clearly identified as a separate bounded context rather than being embedded in content-manager-service.

gapAnalysis.title: ContentObjectStatus as untyped string constants with no state machine
gapAnalysis.detail: ContentObjectStatus is a class holding string constants (STATUS_READY, STATUS_FAILED, STATUS_UPLOAD_POST_UPLOAD_PROCESSING, etc.) with a raw string Status property. There is no enforcement of valid transitions, no exhaustive enum for compile-time safety, and status comparisons use raw string equality throughout the codebase. This should be a proper enum or sealed class with allowed-transition logic.

gapAnalysis.title: Exception types are ad-hoc custom classes not mapped through a DomainExceptionType enum
gapAnalysis.detail: The codebase has 20+ ad-hoc exception classes (FileNotFoundException, NoPermissionException, DuplicateNameException, SchedulePublishTaskNotFoundException, etc.) each inheriting from ContentManagerException or NuPitchRequestException. There is no central DomainExceptionType enum to map to HTTP status codes, making error-handling middleware complex and HTTP status decisions scattered. A unified exception pattern would allow a single ExceptionFilter to handle all domain exceptions.
gapAnalysis.file: ContentManagerException.cs, FileNotFoundException.cs, NoPermissionException.cs, DuplicateNameException.cs (and 15+ others in LibraryService.Abstractions/Exceptions/)

gapAnalysis.title: Cart pattern in Orchestrator accumulates context without explicit aggregate identity
gapAnalysis.detail: The Cart class (Seismic.ContentManager.Express.Orchestrator/Cart/Cart.cs) is passed through every Checkpoint chain and Writer to accumulate validated data (file, user, folder). This is a mutable bag-of-objects pattern that obscures which aggregates are loaded and what state has been validated. It conflates the loaded domain objects with the validation context, making it hard to reason about what has been verified at any point in the flow.
